title: Question 4
stem:
A small crystal is made to vibrate with simple harmonic motion. The variation with time $t$ of the displacement $x$ of one surface of the crystal from its equilibrium position is shown in Fig. 4.1.

{{figure:figure_4_1}}

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Show that the angular frequency of the vibration of the surface is $4.2 \times 10^7 \text{rad s}^{-1}$.
hints: Hint 1: Look at Fig. 4.1 and count how long one complete vibration takes - pick the same point on two neighbouring peaks to find the period $T$.
Hint 2: Remember how the time for one cycle links to how fast the phase angle advances, then convert the $10^{-6}\text{ s}$ scale carefully.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Read the period from the graph**
Think of one full back-and-forth as the time between two identical points. In Fig. 4.1 the peaks repeat every $0.15 \times 10^{-6}\text{ s}$. For example peaks near $0.04$, $0.19$, $0.34$, $0.49$ in units of $10^{-6}\text{ s}$ all differ by $0.15$. So $$T = 0.15 \times 10^{-6}\text{ s}$$

Step 2: **Convert period to angular frequency**
For any SHM, one cycle is $2\pi$ radians of phase, so $$\omega = \frac{2\pi}{T}$$ Put the numbers in: $$\omega = \frac{2\pi}{0.15 \times 10^{-6}} \approx 4.19 \times 10^{7}\text{ rad s}^{-1}$$ which is $4.2 \times 10^{7}\text{ rad s}^{-1}$ to 2 s.f.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Determine the maximum acceleration $a_0$ of the vibration of the surface.
hints: Hint 1: Find the largest displacement from equilibrium in Fig. 4.1 - that peak value is the amplitude $x_0$ in metres.
Hint 2: Think about where acceleration is largest in SHM and how it scales with amplitude and how fast the oscillation is.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Get the amplitude**
The top of the sine curve reaches $40$ on the $x/10^{-6}\text{ m}$ axis, so $$x_0 = 40 \times 10^{-6}\text{ m}$$ Acceleration in SHM follows $a = -\omega^2 x$, so its magnitude is biggest at the extremes of motion.

Step 2: **Calculate maximum acceleration**
Use $$a_0 = \omega^2 x_0$$ with $\omega = 4.2 \times 10^{7}\text{ rad s}^{-1}$: $$a_0 = (4.2 \times 10^{7})^2 \times (40 \times 10^{-6})$$ $$a_0 \approx 7.1 \times 10^{10}\text{ m s}^{-2}$$ The value is huge because the frequency is in the MHz range even though the displacement is only micrometres.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The crystal may be modelled as a single mass of $2.4 \times 10^{-4} \text{kg}$ that vibrates as shown in Fig. 4.1.

Calculate the total energy $E$ of the vibrations.
hints: Hint 1: The total energy stays constant and can be evaluated at the moment of maximum displacement where it is all elastic potential - what three quantities must it depend on?
Hint 2: Check the given mass and the amplitude from Fig. 4.1, making sure both are in base SI units of $\text{kg}$ and $\text{m}$.
Hint 3: Combine $m$, $\omega$ from (a) and $x_0$ in the energy expression and evaluate the powers of ten carefully.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Choose the energy formula**
For an SHM mass the kinetic plus potential always adds to $$E = \frac{1}{2}m\omega^2 x_0^2$$ You can think of it as $\frac{1}{2}m v_{max}^2$ since $v_{max} = \omega x_0$. Here $m = 2.4 \times 10^{-4}\text{ kg}$.

Step 2: **Substitute with correct units**
$$E = \frac{1}{2} \times (2.4 \times 10^{-4}) \times (4.2 \times 10^{7})^2 \times (40 \times 10^{-6})^2$$

Step 3: **Evaluate**
$(4.2 \times 10^{7})^2 = 1.76 \times 10^{15}$ and $(40 \times 10^{-6})^2 = 1.6 \times 10^{-9}$. So $$E \approx 0.5 \times 2.4 \times 10^{-4} \times 1.76 \times 10^{15} \times 1.6 \times 10^{-9} \approx 340\text{ J}$$ to 2 s.f.

parts.label: (d)
parts.part_stem: The crystal generates ultrasound waves that are used to obtain diagnostic information about internal structures.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.text:
The crystal is made from piezoelectric material.

Explain how the crystal is made to vibrate.

markscheme_points.text: applying p.d. to / across crystal causes it to distort

hints: Hint 1: A piezoelectric crystal changes shape when it feels an electric field - so what electrical signal must you put across its faces to make it move?
Hint 2: To keep it vibrating millions of times per second at ultrasound frequency, think about what type of voltage would repeatedly reverse the distortion.
parts.proper_answer: Apply an alternating p.d. across the crystal. The p.d. causes the piezoelectric crystal to distort, so the alternating polarity makes it vibrate at the frequency of the applied p.d.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Link voltage to shape change**
A piezoelectric material is special because an applied p.d. across it makes the lattice strain - it expands or contracts a little. The faces move as charge appears on them.

Step 2: **Make the distortion oscillate**
If you apply an alternating p.d. across the crystal, the direction of distortion reverses every half cycle. The crystal is therefore forced to vibrate continuously, generating ultrasound at the drive frequency.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
A parallel beam of ultrasound waves is incident on a muscle-bone boundary. Data for muscle and bone are given in Table 4.1.

Table 4.1

| material | $\text{density} / \text{kg m}^{-3}$ | $\text{speed of sound} / \text{m s}^{-1}$ |
| muscle | 1100 | 1600 |
| bone | 1900 | 4100 |

Calculate the percentage of the intensity of the ultrasound beam that is transmitted at this boundary.
hints: Hint 1: The amount reflected at a boundary depends on how different the two media are acoustically - start by combining density and sound speed for each material.
Hint 2: Think about the formula that uses the difference and sum of those two acoustic values to give the reflected fraction of intensity.
Hint 3: Remember transmitted plus reflected must add to 100%, so subtract your reflected percentage from the whole.
parts.proper_answer: $Z_m = 1100 \times 1600 = 1.76 \times 10^{6}\text{ kg m}^{-2}\text{s}^{-1}$, $Z_b = 1900 \times 4100 = 7.79 \times 10^{6}\text{ kg m}^{-2}\text{s}^{-1}$. Reflected fraction $= [(Z_b-Z_m)/(Z_b+Z_m)]^2 \approx 0.40$. Percentage transmitted $\approx 60\%$.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Calculate acoustic impedances**
Impedance tells you how hard it is for sound to pass through: $$Z = \rho c$$ So $$Z_{muscle} = 1100 \times 1600 = 1.76 \times 10^{6}$$ $$Z_{bone} = 1900 \times 4100 = 7.79 \times 10^{6}$$ in $\text{kg m}^{-2}\text{s}^{-1}$.

Step 2: **Find reflected intensity fraction**
For normal incidence: $$\frac{I_r}{I} = \left(\frac{Z_b - Z_m}{Z_b + Z_m}\right)^2$$ $$\frac{I_r}{I} = \left(\frac{7.79 - 1.76}{7.79 + 1.76}\right)^2 = \left(\frac{6.03}{9.55}\right)^2 \approx 0.40$$ So about $40\%$ is reflected.

Step 3: **Convert to transmitted percentage**
Energy is conserved at the boundary, so $$\text{transmitted } \% = 100\% - 40\% = 60\%$$
